notes:
- **Heeler's own RAW decoder.** Every RAW file Heeler opens is now read and developed by a decoder written for Heeler, in place of the library it used before. It reads most cameras' sensor data in half the time or less. For most cameras the pixels it reads are exactly the ones the old decoder read. [Source](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/source/).
- **A spot light in Depth Lighting.** A third kind of light beside the sun and the lamp: a spot stands at one place and depth and points at another, lighting only inside its cone, with a dial for how wide the cone opens and how soft its edge is. Its cone is drawn on the photograph where it lands. [Depth Lighting](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/depth-lighting/).
- **A second depth model for detail inside a subject.** The Depth Map section has a new **Model** menu beside Detail: **DA3 LARGE** (Depth Anything 3 Mono Large) reads the relief inside a subject, a face, a beak, the edge of a wing, where V2 Small gives it its outline. It takes about four times as long and is an optional 433 MB download, asked for the first time you choose it. Each photograph keeps its own model, and Preferences, **Models** sets the one new photographs start with. Photographs you have already edited stay on V2 Small and look exactly as before. Desktop only. [Depth Map](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/depth-map/).
- **Model normals for Depth Lighting.** Depth Lighting's new **Normals: Model** reads which way each surface faces with a second, optional model, so walls light as flat planes, round subjects shade round to their edges, and silhouettes lose the bright or dark rim the depth map's estimate could draw. [Depth Lighting](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/depth-lighting/).
- **More natural color under warm light.** A camera's color now comes from its calibrations for both daylight and tungsten light, blended for the light the photograph was taken in, instead of from the daylight one alone. Photographs taken indoors or at dusk come out closer to the scene. [Source](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/source/).
- **Cleaner smart selections.** Click, Subject and Sky now use Segment Anything 2.1, with cleaner edges and thin parts that hold together. It is a new 156 MB download the first time a Smart tool asks for it. Selections made in earlier versions keep the model they were made with, so documents open exactly as they were saved; a **SAM 2.1** button beside the mode buttons remakes one with the new model. [Masks and selections](https://www.heeler.app/docs/finish/masks-selections/#the-model-behind-a-smart-selection).
- **Select by text.** Type what to select, "the red car" or "the dog on the left", in the Smart tool's new text field and press Return: the picture reader finds it and Segment Anything selects it. Several matches are offered by number, from the left, or all together, and clicks refine the result. The phrase and what it found are kept with the selection, so it is made the same way everywhere. It uses Florence-2, the assistant's optional 970 MB picture reader. [Masks and selections](https://www.heeler.app/docs/finish/masks-selections/#select-by-text).
- **Navigator and Loupe.** Two new viewing aids. The Navigator (**View > Navigator**) puts a thumbnail of the whole photograph in a corner of the canvas while you are zoomed in past it, with a rectangle for what the canvas shows: drag it to move the view, or click to jump there. **View > Navigator Position**, or a right-click on the Navigator, chooses the corner, and Preferences sets its size. The Loupe, a new button on the viewer's toolbar, is a magnifying glass that follows the pointer, with its magnification printed below it: press `L` to bring it up, scroll or use the zoom keys to change how much it magnifies, and hold `Cmd` (`Ctrl` on Windows) while scrolling to change its size. It shows the photograph's full-resolution pixels even when the canvas is zoomed out. Tools and clicks work through it, and `Esc` puts it down. [Image viewport](https://www.heeler.app/docs/image-viewport/#navigator-and-loupe).
- **Lens Flare from the photograph's own lights.** Lens Flare's new **Bright spots** source finds the street lamps, headlights or sun in the photograph and flares them, with no Depth Lighting and no lights to place. Threshold, Sources, Min size and Spot strength choose which spots flare, and the spots found are listed with a switch each, so one that should not flare can be switched off. **Rig lights** keeps flaring Depth Lighting's lights, and both can be on. A flare from an earlier version opens as Rig lights alone and looks as it did. [Lens Flare](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/depth-lighting/#lens-flare).
- **View depth fitted to the subject.** The Depth Map section's new **Subject** chip spreads the depth view's grays over your subject's own depth, so the relief inside a face or a beak shows even when the subject is a small part of the scene. [Depth Map](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/depth-map/).
- **Your own tone curve.** The Tone Profile has a **Custom** mode: draw the curve from scene light to display in an editor that works like Curves, with Smooth, Linear and Tangent shapes and handles to steer it, or import one from a 1D .cube, a two-column text file or a DNG or camera profile, and save it as a profile that lists in the Profile menu. The curve travels in the document, so it renders the same on a computer without the profile file. [Source](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/source/#tone-profile).
- **A finer Subject matte.** **Subject** now answers with BiRefNet dynamic, which reads fur and fine edges better than the model before it, with soft edges in one shot. It is an optional 972 MB download, asked for the first time you use Subject. Selections made in earlier versions keep the matte they had. [Masks and selections](https://www.heeler.app/docs/finish/masks-selections/#the-subject-matte).
- **A rotation ring on the crop.** With the crop tool up, drag along the dashed ring around the crop, or anywhere outside it, and the picture turns as the pointer goes round, against a level grid. Double-click the ring to level it again. [Geometry](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/geometry/#rotation-ring).
- **Straightening keeps a clean crop.** With **Stay inside picture** on, as it is by default, straightening shrinks the crop so no empty corner shows, and coming back to level gives the whole frame again. **Crop to picture** sets the largest crop that is all picture in one click. [Geometry](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/geometry/#crop-to-picture).
- **Film crop ratios.** The crop bar's ratio menu has the cinema's widths in their own group, named by their decimals: 1.85, 2.00, 2.35, 2.39, 2.40, 2.50 and 2.76, and a ratio of your own can be typed with decimals. [Geometry](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/geometry/#crop-ratios).
- **Panoramas line up at their edges.** Each frame's lens distortion is undone from its lens profile before the frames are matched, so wide frames line up across the whole overlap rather than only its middle. The Pano panel says which profile was found, and **Lens correction** turns it off. [Panoramas](https://www.heeler.app/docs/composites/#lens-correction).
- **Seams that go round what moved.** Where frames overlap, the seam now runs where they agree, through sky, grass or anything that stayed still, and around anything that moved between the shots. Someone walking through the overlap, or a car driving across it, appears once and whole, not cut in half, doubled or left as a faint copy. [Panoramas](https://www.heeler.app/docs/composites/#seams).
- **Panoramas open cropped.** A new panorama opens with Crop & Rotate set to the largest rectangle it fills, an ordinary crop you can widen again. **Auto-crop** in the Pano panel turns it off and on without stitching again. [Panoramas](https://www.heeler.app/docs/composites/#auto-crop).
- **Point lights and spots light the scene like lamps.** In Depth Lighting, a point light or a spot now adds its light onto what it lands on rather than multiplying the light already there, so a lamp aimed at a dark street at night throws a visible pool of light. On a scene lit about middle gray it looks as before; on darker scenes it is stronger, on brighter ones weaker. Edits with these lights look different where the scene is darker or brighter than that. [Depth Lighting](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/depth-lighting/).
- **Merge and panorama files are YAML.** A new `.stack` or `.pano` file is saved as YAML, the same readable format as presets, with the line named when one cannot be read. Files from earlier versions open as before and become YAML the next time the merge or panorama is changed. [Merges and panoramas](https://www.heeler.app/docs/composites/#the-recipe-file).
- **The lines over the photograph are white.** The crop box, the warp grids and rings, and the Radial and Linear layers' outlines draw in white rather than a color chosen from the photograph, and a color picker replaces the Hue and Luma sliders. **Preferences > Interface** sets the starting color, and **Automatic line color** there brings back the color chosen from the photograph. [Grid Warp](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/grid-warp/#the-lines-color).
- **Colors shift a little.** Because of the new color, photographs you have already edited can look slightly different, most of all those taken under tungsten light. For about 200 cameras, among them Olympus and OM System, Pentax, Samsung, Phase One, Leaf and Kodak bodies and some Panasonic and Sony ones, the color in daylight changes a little too, since Heeler now uses the same calibrations for them as for every other camera. Your edits are kept; check the color on a photograph that matters before exporting it again. [Source](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/source/).
- **Fujifilm X-Trans photographs use Heeler's own demosaic at full size.** Fine detail and edges against a bright sky can look very slightly different from before. [Source](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/source/).
- **Highlights: Rebuild and the Demosaic menu are gone.** A photograph edited with Rebuild now develops with Clip, and one edited with the Fast or Fine demosaic develops with Heeler's demosaic. [Source](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/source/#raw-controls).
- **A camera newer than Heeler says so.** A RAW file from a camera Heeler does not know yet shows its thumbnail and says "this camera is not supported yet", instead of developing with guessed color. An update that adds the camera develops it. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/#raw-files-heeler-cannot-develop-yet).
- **A few rare older formats no longer develop.** The Nikon D1X's compressed NEF, the YI action cameras' first DNGs, the FinePix F700's RAF, the GX680 digital back's RAF, the DSC-F828's SRF, the Kodak DC50's KDC, the Minolta RD175's MDC and some action cameras' .RAW files show their thumbnails but do not open for editing. Converting them to DNG with a converter that reads them works in the meantime. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/#raw-files-heeler-cannot-develop-yet).
- **Match exposure in the Pano panel works.** Switching **Match exposure** off in the Pano panel wrote the panorama's recipe back unchanged, so the switch stayed on however often it was clicked. It now takes effect, as do the new **Lens correction** and **Auto-crop** switches. [Panoramas](https://www.heeler.app/docs/composites/#panoramas).
- **A drag off the canvas leaves the panels alone.** A straighten line, a crop edge or a brush stroke carried off the canvas could move a slider it crossed in the panel, so a straighten drag could set the Color section's Temp. Sliders, the Harmony wheel and the compare split now follow only a drag that began on them. [Image viewport](https://www.heeler.app/docs/image-viewport/).
